subject: Interactive plots not working, showing [object Object]

messages.author: 7d8a24ae49d0dcb1
messages.subject: Interactive plots not working, showing [object Object]
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to get started with ggvis, and for me the interactive plots aren't working.  None of them.

I cut/paste in line after line from the demos and examples, and where ever interactive components are supposed to appear, I only get a grey bar with the text "[object Object]" within.  The plots show up just fine (with default values for the interactive ones).  Sample screen clip attached.

I'm on a Mac, and I just installed the new public release of RStudio, I installed R 3.1 (Previously I was on 3.0.2) and re-installed devtools, github versions of shiny, ggvis, ggplot2, dplyr, and data.table from CRAN.

Same results in both RStudio and in command-line R (from a Terminal window), same results in both Safari and in Chrome, and in RStudio's Viewer window.  Safari's web inspector shows no errors, but a few warnings are shown:

Invalid CSS property declaration at: * (bootstrap.min.css:9)
Invalid CSS property declaration at: * (bootstrap-responsive.min.css:9)

I'm really not a web developer, so I really don't even know how to debug it at all.  I've googled with absolutely no results for several hours now, and so I'm posting here in the hopes that if anyone else experiences this problem they can find a solution easier!

Can anyone help me?

Thanks in advance,

Trenton Tuggle

I get exactly the same behaviour on ubuntu saucy (13.10) with R version 3.1.0 (2014-04-10), ggvis version 0.1.0.99, shiny version 0.9.1.9005 and testthat version 0.8.1.0.99.

~TK

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Interactive plots not working, showing [object Object]
parts:
Hi guys -
Sorry that you're running into this problem. There seems to be some incompatibility with ggvis and the development version of Shiny, but it should work with the CRAN version of Shiny.

There are some fairly large changes to ggvis in the works - this issue will be fixed, but bear in mind that the ggvis API will also change. Working with a changing API isn't ideal, but it'll be worth it!

-Winston
